title: Pirated recordings and uncollected royalties
summary: Hinton and Budd discuss wire-recorded party tapings sold in Europe and royalties musicians never knew to collect.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: By the way there was a lot of thievery going on, a lot of parties given, people had wire recordings.

You better believe it. These little old Webster wire recorders, and it would -- you know, actually it's a whole lot of stuff been kettled into the European countries. You might be sitting up you say hey, that sounds like me. And it was probably something you did at a party.
Well, in Europe you know they'll buy anything like somebody with some name on it, and they'll clean

it up and they'll just put out a certain amount of these things, maybe 1500 of them, collector's items. And people just to say like they have some Bird records when he was first here, had some of your records when you first did something, or -- and they can get these names --
And you didn't get a dime out of it.

We never got a dime out of it. I think maybe one day, but you know this is a very complicated thing. I'm just learning now that you have to belong to all of these different societies all over the world in order to collect.

But they have a little tighter thing. If there's anything you ever done in France or Germany or England, that money is still there waiting for you to just collect it if you join one of these societies. You know? And --
Most of us didn't know anything about it.
No, of course not. I mean, I was writing for writing's sake, you know, I was playing, just happy to be playing --
-- with certain cats. And you know, we had a difficult enough time just trying to keep up with

what's going on and learning how to play your instrument rather than to try to be a businessman with a lawyer and all of that sort of thing. Because you know, that's what you're dealing with, you're dealing with cats that knows all about business administration, knows about law when you're talking to him. If he doesn't here's a guy sitting in his presence listening to what you say, he's a lawyer or something. So I mean, it's just a trickery thing.
This business is all trickery, I mean it's fortunes been made off of us that we'll probably never get. Maybe --
There's a lot of thievery going on and we could call it that now.
